manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the bottle on the table and lift it.

Task description: The target is the white bottle lying horizontally on the left side of the table with a light-colored cap. Grasp it with the right gripper, lift it off the table, and orient it to a nearly upright pose with the cap facing upward.

Success criteria: The bottle is held by the gripper and lifted as a whole off the table, with its body nearly vertical, cap up and bottom down; lifting it while horizontal does not count as completion.

## Execution tips

- Consider gripping the side wall around the middle of the bottle, where its diameter is fairly uniform, with the fingers closing toward each other across its long axis. Avoid the cap, shoulder, and bottom edge to reduce slipping or rotation.
- During approach, open slightly wider than the grasp section and confirm both fingers lie on opposite bottle sides with effective sidewall contact. Leave fingertip-to-table clearance to avoid pressing the table or rolling the bottle away.
- To turn the bottle cap upward, make a small rotation where there is enough clearance between the bottle and table, watching the base's swing to avoid sweeping it across the table.
- If the bottle slides along the pads while lifting or rotating, first let it rest on the table again before adjusting the grasp, avoiding a drop from releasing it while suspended.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start only this physical-robot episode with the specified parameters, operate from the returned manual and live observations, and call finish_episode upon completion or inability to continue.

The target is confirmed as the white bottle lying on the left, with only the right arm available. The gripper is open and I am adjusting the approach pose. After grasping I will check the hold, lift, and gradually turn it cap-up.
Approach pose feedback is normal, and the bottle remains in its original position. I am aligning with the middle of the body and adjusting the gripper angle before contact.
The gripper is nearly aligned with the bottle’s long axis and is descending in steps of no more than 1 cm. I am checking clearance between the pads, bottle body, and table at each step.

The fingers are on opposite sides of the bottle, with an opening of approximately 65 mm. Next I will tighten the grasp and first test-lift 1 cm to check whether it leaves the table steadily with the gripper.
The bottle slipped between the pads during the test lift and returned to the table; no stable grasp was formed. Within this episode, I will open, realign with the body and lower the grasp position.
The bottle has been realigned. This time I will put the pads deeper on opposite sides of its body and test-lift in small steps to confirm grasp stability.

During this test lift, the bottle rose with the gripper, the opening remained around 62.6 mm and the previous sliding was absent. Next I will increase table clearance and gradually rotate the cap upward.
The entire bottle is off the table and remains between the fingers during rotation. I am continuing small-angle adjustments toward cap-up. Afterward I will observe it at rest, then end the episode.

During further rotation, the controller reported a recoverable singularity rejection. The arm moved slightly, and the bottle remains grasped. I will adjust position using the returned actual pose, then try turning it upright again.
After adjusting position, motion resumed normally, and the bottle remains securely grasped. I will continue adjusting height to leave room for the final rotation.
The bottle cap is up, but its body is still tilted. The grasp remains stable. I will complete the remaining angle adjustment and check the final state using the wrist image and measured pose.
The previous large upward movement reached the workspace limit, so I reduced it to a smaller movement within the allowable range. The bottle remains in the gripper; only a pose adjustment remains.

After a stationary observation, the bottle remains grasped. Based on the wrist image, continuous holding state, and measured pose, I assess that it is off the table and nearly vertical, cap up and bottom down. I will now end this episode; final success is for the on-site operator to confirm.
